title: Quant kernel safety matrix and runtime guidance
body:
Purpose
This note collects operational constraints and a lightweight compatibility/safety matrix for quantized execution paths (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) inside the serving runtime. Aim is to make rollout decisions deterministic: when a request should take a quantized kernel, when to coerce precision, and when to fallback to a higher-precision fast path.

Audience
Serving runtime engineers, kernel authors, SRE on-call, and product owners evaluating rollout risk for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Scope and assumptions
- Focus on model architectures in active use (decoder-only GPT variants, encoder-decoder for retrieval, and Llama-family derivatives).
- Not covering per-token output quant adjustments (post-token rounding) — this is about weights/activation quant paths and KV cache interactions.
- We assume the runtime can select kernels per-layer and apply on-the-fly type conversion for inputs/outputs.

High-level goals
- Safety: avoid silent correctness regressions (wrong logits, broken attention) due to incompatible kernels or precision mismatch.
- Predictability: minimizing variance in latency when switching between quantized and fallback paths.
- Cost control: allow quantized paths when unit-economics benefit > configured threshold.
- Rollout friendliness: enable gradual canaries, canary-by-model-version and canary-by-route.

Operational primitives implemented in runtime (reference)
- KernelCapability: per-kernel descriptor listing supported quant formats, supported op shapes (transposed/not), memory alignment requirements, and numeric stability flags.
- LayerProfile: per-model-layer metadata (weight-format, transposed, fused-bias, require-layernorm-accum in FP32).
- PrecisionFence: a runtime boundary where conversions to FP32 must occur (e.g., pre-LN residual adds, fused-attn-softmax boundaries).
- KVCacheDescriptor: describes in-storage precision, max-shard-size, and conversion cost estimates.
- FallbackPolicy: declarative rules (latency-sensitive, accuracy-sensitive, conservative) mapping to allowed KernelCapability sets.

Safety matrix (operational view)
Columns: Operation, Typical kernel shape constraints, INT8 safe?, FP8 safe?, GPTQ safe?, AWQ safe?, Notes
- MatMul (weight dense): contiguous weights, row-major preferred; INT8: conditional (per-channel requant + scale table present), FP8: supported if activation conversions applied, GPTQ: supported if dequantization operator available and per-block scale metadata preserved, AWQ: supported only for non-transposed weights with AWQ meta present. Note: transposed weight layouts commonly used in older checkpoints require reordering or specialized kernels.
- Attention (QK + O projections): fused QKV best; INT8: not recommended for fused QKV unless fused kernel supports per-head scaling, FP8: generally ok for projections but softmax must be FP32, GPTQ: QKV projections ok if scales stored per-block, AWQ: OK for O projection if layout matches.
- LayerNorm: requires FP32 accumulation; INT8/FP8 kernels are only allowed for pre/post reductions if accumulation in FP32 implemented. GPTQ/AWQ: not applicable for LayerNorm weights (usually scale/shift small).
- Softmax: must run in FP32 for numerical stability (even if inputs are stored quantized). Always create a PrecisionFence around softmax.
- GELU/Activation: INT8/FP8 acceptable if approximations are numerically validated; prefer FP16/FP32 if model is accuracy-sensitive.
- Embedding lookup: quantized table ok (INT8/FP8) but requires upcast to FP32 before accumulation across sparse indices.

Kernel constraints (detailed)
- Alignment: INT8 kernels require 16 byte alignment of weight blocks, or performance degrades severely. Runtime must ensure buffer allocation with pad.
- Block sizes: GPTQ/AWQ kernels assume block-quantization metadata at 32xN block granularity. If model quant metadata deviates, mark as incompatible.
- Transposed weights: many older HuggingFace checkpoints store transposed linear weights. Quant kernels typically expect packed contiguous layout matching inference runtime. Provide a conversion step during model upload, but mark conversion cost in LayerProfile.
- Fused ops: fused GatedLinearUnit or fused attention kernels must advertise exact op signature (bias present/absent, post-mul scaling). Mismatch -> fallback.
- Accumulators: any reduction that sums across large dims must specify accumulator precision. If accumulator is FP32 we can use INT8 inputs; if only FP16 available we must test.

KV cache and quantization interactions
- Cache precision: we prefer storing KV cache in the serving-node native compute precision (FP16 or FP32) to avoid repeated conversions. If model path uses INT8/FP8 kernels, cache writes may require dequantization to FP16/FP32 and re-quantization on read for certain kernels.
- Prefix caching: when prefix tokens were generated with a different model precision or quant path than current runtime selection, we must mark the cache as precision-mismatched and either (a) convert cache on-the-fly (costly), (b) force fallback to compatible kernel, or (c) maintain multiple cache variants per precision — config controls this.
- Cache invalidation: when model version changes quant metadata (e.g., new block sizes), invalidate caches for that model-version.
- Cost model: runtime estimates conversion cost = (bytes moved * conversion factor) + extra kernel latency. Use conservative multiplier 1.5x memory copy for initial rollout.

Scheduling considerations
- Kernel affinity: maintain per-GPU kernel affinity tables. Some quant kernels are faster on A100 vs H100 due to tensor core ops; store measured latency per-hw+kernel and include in scheduling score.
- Request-level decision: on request arrival, runtime consults (model version -> LayerProfile) + (FSD fallback policy) + (current GPU availability) -> choose per-layer kernel. This means some layers may run quantized and others FP32 in the same request; ensure conversion fences are inserted and accounted for.
- Batching: quant kernels often have different throughput scaling; automatic batching should consider mixed-precision batch composition and prefer homogeneous batches when latency SLO tight.

Fallback policy examples
- Conservative (default for Dedicated/Private initial rollout): only use quant kernels that passed end-to-end canary (see test plan). If any layer lacks KernelCapability for that quant format, run FP16/FP32 path.
- Cost-first (optimize for RU): allow quant kernels if expected token cost reduction > 20% even if a small accuracy delta is possible (requires opt-in per-customer).
- Latency-sensitive: prefer kernels with lowest p99 measured latency; prefer FP16 if quantized path increases tail latency due to conversion fences.

Metrics and signals to monitor
- Per-token latency p50/p95/p99 by kernel type and model version.
- Logit drift: run production shadow eval on small prompt set; measure KL divergence and top-k mismatch rate between quant path and full-precision golden path. Alert threshold: top-1 mismatch > 0.8% or KL > 0.02 for canonical prompts.
- Error rates: kernel throws, OOMs, misaligned buffers. Track per-instance.
- KV cache conversion rate: fraction of requests requiring cache precision conversion.

Test plan and canary checklist
- Unit: per-kernel unit tests validating numerical range, saturation behavior, and alignment handling.
- Integration: run sample-generation tests across model family matrix with reference outputs (golden FP32 outputs). Compute top-k and KL stats.
- Canary rollout steps: 1) internal service canary (5% traffic) with shadow golden path, 2) enterprise customer opt-in, 3) broader gradual ramp with automatic rollback on metric regressions.

Runtime implementation notes / TODOs
- Add KernelCapability schema to model manifest and include quant metadata in model upload flow (RI-2571).
- Implement precision fence insertion optimizer that minimizes conversion count across request graph (prototype in branch quant-fences-aug2026).
- Measure conversion cost on H100 and A100 and publish numbers in kernel catalogue (measurement ticket GH-934).
- Add an automated preflight job that validates uploaded quant metadata and optionally performs layout conversion (JIRA-RI-2345).

Open questions
- For AWQ-like methods which require specific layout/metadata, should we maintain a small on-disk cache of converted artifacts per model version? Tradeoff: disk vs upload time.
- Should we allow mixed-block-size GPTQ metadata within the same model? If yes, we need kernel support and more complex LayerProfile validation.
- How to present precision decisions to customers in Console (transparent trace vs opaque automated)?

Appendix: example LayerProfile snippet (human readable)
- layer: 12_attention.q_proj
  weight-layout: packed-row
  quant-format: GPTQ
  block-size: 32
  transposed: false
  requires-accumulation: FP32

References and prior art
- AWQ paper notes and kernel reference (internal reading list)
- GPTQ repo (adaptation notes)

If you want, I can transform this into a checklist-style runbook for canaries or produce a short slide deck for the SRE onboarding. Next steps I recommend: assign RI-2571 for manifest changes and schedule a 2-week spike to implement the precision-fence optimizer.
